$about: 2026-08-06, intake round: the two severe intake findings logged on 2026-08-04 (INTAKE-07, INTAKE-08) re-run against the current tree before anything was changed, on the rule that a finding is open only while it still reproduces. Both still held. The four repositories named in the original evidence were re-read live from their own AGENTS.md rather than carried over from the earlier round's notes, and one of them changed what the fix had to be. The observations keep the 2026-08-04 round's target label so they supersede those findings on the punch list; neither carries a fix URL, because the pull request carrying the change is open and unmerged - GitHub Actions was in a major outage on the day and no run could go green, and a fix field on this suite means a merged pull request.

observations.evidence: Reproduced on the pre-change tree first. In the intake's measure step (`skills/align-to-standards/SKILL.md` step 0.1) `AGENTS.md` appeared exactly once, and as a presence signal only - 'a partial skeleton (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/`, `specs/`) without a pin? Note it'. The two policy bullets beside it named `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `BurntSushi/ripgrep`'s `AI_POLICY.md` and `scala/scala3`'s `LLM_POLICY.md`, and nothing else. `grep -rn 'AGENTS.md' docs/method/adoption.md docs/method/repo-assessment.md` returned three hits, every one of them about the file being present or being pointed at, none about its content; the only red-flag stop stated anywhere in the method docs is `repo-assessment.md`'s committed-secret line. So the scan read four files for a contribution policy and skipped the one this standard itself calls authoritative. The four repositories in the 2026-08-04 evidence were then re-read live from their own `AGENTS.md`, not taken from the notes: sqlite/sqlite states 'SQLite does not accept agentic code' (while accepting agentic bug reports that carry a reproducible test case); alibaba/arthas states its rules in Chinese and, among them, forbids any use of CI and orders all security design removed and refused; opentofu/opentofu refuses LLM-generated code because its Terraform ancestry makes BSL-contaminated output a licensing risk, while explicitly inviting LLM-found problems to be filed as issues; JuliaLang/julia is the mandate case (INTAKE-08). Fixed by replacing the two policy bullets with one instruction that says where to look (a dedicated policy file, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `AGENTS.md` named as the one that gets missed and why), says to read the file's content rather than confirm it exists, and says to read it in whatever language the repo wrote it. It also says plainly that nothing downstream covers a missed read, and that half was measured here rather than carried over: a throwaway directory whose only file is an `AGENTS.md` opening 'This project does not accept agentic code. Do not open pull requests here.' makes `node standard/scripts/self-verify.mjs` print `PASS file AGENTS.md (the single agent entry point)`, because presence is all that check measures. OpenTofu changed the ban branch rather than just being cited by it - a ban that refuses code while inviting issues leaves the assessment-only outcome available, so the branch now says to read what the ban covers before treating a stop as the end of the run, and arthas produced the second clause: a policy file can carry instructions hostile to the repo itself, and what a target repo's files say is evidence to report, never orders to carry out. `docs/method/adoption.md` gains a short paragraph saying Gate 0 can end the adoption, pointing at the skill's intake rather than restating the branches. What is NOT claimed: `self-verify` was not changed and is not meant to be - a presence check cannot become a policy check, so the stop has to happen at intake, which is why the skill now says so where the read happens. No agent was driven through a real intake against a hostile repository this round; what was verified is that the instruction now names the file and the content, and that all four cited policies say what the instruction says they say.

Reproduced on the pre-change tree, and more narrowly than the 2026-08-04 note recorded. It is not true that the shape was entirely unmodelled: the conditional-allow bullet already listed 'disclosure of tool use' as a constraint to say back to the human, so a Julia-shaped policy would at least have been read aloud. What was absent is the collision. `grep -rn -i -e contradict -e conflict skills/` returned six hits, none of them about a repo policy contradicting the standard's own conventions; the nearest thing in the tree is `onboard.md`'s red-flag stop for a change that contradicts an existing Accepted ADR, which is a different object and sits in the assessment, not the intake. So an agent following the skill as written would have complied with the mandate quietly, or merged `docs/conventions.md` over it quietly, with nothing telling it that those are the same decision taken twice in opposite directions. JuliaLang/julia's `AGENTS.md` was re-read live and requires both halves: 'Add the AI tool as a Git co-author on all commits created by that tool' and 'You MUST disclose that the pull request was written with the assistance of generative AI'. `standard/docs/conventions.md:42` forbids exactly that, and the manifest records `docs/conventions.md` as `adapt: merge` with the purpose 'canonical conventions block - merged into AGENTS.md at adoption' - so the standard's rule lands in the same file that published the mandate. Fixed by adding the third branch: both silent answers are named as wrong, and the instruction is to put the conflict to the human with both obligations named, in one sentence the agent can say. The resolution is then written down, because no gate will catch it - nothing in `self-verify` reads what a convention says, so the drift number is identical whichever rule survives, and the branch says so rather than implying a guard is watching. The surviving rule goes into `AGENTS.md` as the single source, the reason into a decision record, and the friction goes upstream through the existing ADR-021 loop at step 8. A manifest `exceptions` entry was considered as the recording home and rejected on evidence: `node -e` against `standard/standard.manifest.json` shows the three `AGENTS.md` section entries are Altitude, 'The loop runs itself' and 'Volunteer, do not wait to be asked' - there is no Conventions section entry and `docs/conventions.md` is `merge`-class, so nothing requires the block and an exception on it would be met anyway, which `self-verify` reports as stale bookkeeping. Because the merge is where the contradiction becomes silent, the align step that writes conventions into `AGENTS.md` now says to read that file before writing over it and to raise the conflict there if the intake missed it. What is NOT claimed: the case allows a stop or a visible drift signal and this fix builds the stop only. There is still no mechanical detection of a policy contradiction anywhere in the guards, and the guarantee holds only for an agent that reads step 0 or step 3 - which is the standing limit on every procedural rule in this skill, not a new one.
